chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah and others, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) freed the worst of his slaves upon his death and kept the best of them. I said to him, 'O Father, why do you free these and keep these?' He said, 'They have struck me, so this [freedom] is for that [striking].'
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Baqir free the worst slaves and keep the best ones?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) demonstrates a nuanced approach to manumission by freeing the 'inferior' slaves who had struck him, viewing their physical exertion as a form of service justifying their release, while retaining the 'superior' ones. This incident highlights the Shia scholarly understanding of *ijtirah* (manumission for service) and the Imam's personal discretion in determining the value of a slave's contribution. It serves as a practical precedent for how masters may evaluate the merits of slaves when deciding upon emancipation.
